corpus.tau_rule: exact mean cosine over all unordered corpus pairs

holdout.tau_rule: exact mean cosine over all unordered corpus pairs

bootstrap.method: item bootstrap, percentile interval; paired across runs with the same corpus and seed; scheme tree re-induced per resample; ref_cost_norm held at its full-sample value

placement: one isolated store per scheme and tier with an empty rules file; low-confidence placements kept; fallback placements (no candidate) counted as unplaced

runtime.scheme_builds: about 1 min for 13 schemes (fetch, compile and build; every file sha256 equal to 2026-10-10)
runtime.average_linkage_baseline: not recomputed: ref_cost_norm taken from ../2026-10-10/results.json after checking each graph_sha256
runtime.concurrency: at most 3 placement jobs at once over all tiers; tiers run one after another (shortlist, rerank, lexical); each semantic batch pinned to its own 5 CPUs (--cpus-per-job 5), bootstrap scoring on 2 threads (--score-threads 2)
runtime.shortlist: about 2 h 35 min for 19 jobs: lcc-full alone first (36 min, to measure memory), then the other 18, 3 at a time (1 h 58 min); classify_seconds sum 23,071, longest 2,058 (lcc-full corpus)
runtime.rerank: about 2 h 16 min for 19 jobs, 3 at a time; classify_seconds sum 23,110, longest 3,246
runtime.lexical: about 20 min for 19 jobs, 3 at a time; classify_seconds sum 1,470, longest 895 (lcc-full corpus)
runtime.peak_memory: 8.0 GiB summed RSS over all running shelfmark and harness processes (sampled every 5 s); the largest single process was the rerank lcc-full holdout batch at 6.9 GiB, which loads the store's 1.46 GB memo.jsonl left by the lcc-full corpus batch; a semantic corpus batch held about 1.2 GiB and a bootstrap scoring run at most 0.44 GiB
runtime.total_wall_clock: about 5 h 10 min of placement and scoring on 16 CPUs, 31 GiB RAM
